questions.question: A screen shares a link with this code. What kind of intent is `send`?
options: An implicit intent, resolved by matching its action and MIME type against intent filters
An explicit intent, because it carries an `EXTRA_TEXT` extra with the exact data to share
An explicit intent, because `createChooser` picks the exact target component
A `PendingIntent`, because another app will execute it
questions.explanation: An intent is explicit only when it names a target component (e.g. `Intent(context, DetailActivity::class.java)`). `send` names only `ACTION_SEND` and a type, so it is implicit and resolved against intent filters. Extras and the chooser wrapper don't change that.

questions.question: `IntentService` is still the recommended way for a modern app to run a one-off background task off the main thread.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `IntentService` was deprecated in API 30. Since Android 8 background execution limits it can't be reliably started from the background anyway. Use WorkManager for deferrable work, or a coroutine for work tied to a screen.

questions.question: On an app targeting Android 11+, `intent.resolveActivity(packageManager)` returns `null` for a `geo:` map intent even though Google Maps is installed, so the "Open in Maps" button is hidden. Which changes make the feature work correctly?
options: Declare a `<queries>` element in the manifest with an `<intent>` matching the `geo:` VIEW intent
Skip the check: call `startActivity(intent)` directly and catch `ActivityNotFoundException`
Add `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK` to the intent before calling `resolveActivity`
Request the runtime permission for package visibility before resolving
Make the intent explicit by setting the Maps activity class name you expect
questions.explanation: Android 11 package visibility hides other apps from `PackageManager` queries unless you declare them in `<queries>`, so `resolveActivity` returns `null`. Launching the implicit intent still works without `<queries>`, so try/catch is also valid. There is no runtime permission for this, and hard-coding another app's class name is brittle.

questions.question: This models WorkManager's exponential backoff (30 s initial delay, doubling each attempt, capped at 5 hours). What does it print?
questions.code:
const val MAX_BACKOFF = 5 * 60 * 60L

fun backoffSeconds(attempt: Int, initial: Long = 30): Long =
    minOf(initial shl (attempt - 1), MAX_BACKOFF)

fun main() {
    println((1..4).map { backoffSeconds(it) })
    println(backoffSeconds(11))
}
questions.explanation: Attempt `n` waits `30 shl (n - 1)`, so attempts 1..4 give 30, 60, 120, 240 (doubling, not linear). Attempt 11 would be 30 * 1024 = 30720 s, but `minOf` caps it at 18000 s (5 h), like WorkManager's maximum backoff.

questions.question: Which is the current way for an Activity or Fragment to let the user pick a photo and receive the result?
options: Register `registerForActivityResult(PickVisualMedia())` and call `launch(...)` on the launcher
Call `startActivityForResult(intent, REQUEST_CODE)` and override `onActivityResult`
Send a broadcast with `ACTION_PICK` and listen for the reply in a receiver
Create a `PendingIntent` for the gallery and read the result from `Intent` extras in `onResume`
questions.explanation: The Activity Result API (`registerForActivityResult` with a typed contract) replaced `startActivityForResult`/`onActivityResult`, which are deprecated. It gives you a typed callback without request codes. In Compose the equivalent is `rememberLauncherForActivityResult`.

questions.question: Which statements about `PendingIntent` are correct?
options: When targeting Android 12+, creating one without `FLAG_IMMUTABLE` or `FLAG_MUTABLE` throws `IllegalArgumentException`
`FLAG_MUTABLE` is needed when the receiving side must fill in data, such as a notification's inline reply
When it's sent, the wrapped intent runs with the creating app's identity and permissions, even if that app's process has died
`FLAG_IMMUTABLE` still lets the holder replace the target component, just not the extras
`FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT` alone satisfies the Android 12 mutability requirement
questions.explanation: Since Android 12 you must state the mutability explicitly, and `FLAG_IMMUTABLE` should be the default. Use `FLAG_MUTABLE` only when the other side must fill in the intent, e.g. `RemoteInput` replies. An immutable PendingIntent can't be changed at all. `FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT` controls updating extras, not mutability.

questions.question: What happens with this request?
options: It is clamped to the 15-minute minimum and runs roughly every 15 minutes
It runs every 5 minutes exactly as requested
`build()` throws `IllegalArgumentException` because the interval is too short
It runs once and is never repeated
questions.explanation: `PeriodicWorkRequest` has a minimum repeat interval of 15 minutes. A shorter interval doesn't throw: WorkManager logs a warning and uses 15 minutes. For anything more frequent while the user is looking at the screen, use a coroutine loop.

questions.question: On an app targeting Android 12+, an `<activity>` that has an `<intent-filter>` but no explicit `android:exported` attribute makes the app fail to build or install.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Since Android 12, any activity, service or receiver with an intent filter must declare `android:exported` explicitly. Otherwise the build fails (manifest merger error) and the APK can't be installed. Before that, the system silently assumed `true`, which caused accidental exposure.

questions.question: The back stack is A → B → C (all `standard` launch mode). From C you call `startActivity` for A with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP or FLAG_ACTIVITY_SINGLE_TOP`. What happens?
options: B and C finish, and the existing A gets `onNewIntent()`
B and C are finished, and A is destroyed and recreated with the new intent
A new instance of A is pushed on top: A → B → C → A
Only C is finished, giving A → B → A
questions.explanation: `CLEAR_TOP` finishes everything above the existing A. Adding `SINGLE_TOP` makes A, now on top, reuse its instance and get `onNewIntent()`. With `CLEAR_TOP` alone and `standard` launch mode, A itself would also be finished and recreated.

questions.question: A service started with `startService()` and later bound by an Activity is destroyed as soon as that Activity calls `unbindService()`.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A service that is both started and bound stays alive until it is stopped (`stopSelf()`/`stopService()`) AND all clients have unbound. Only a service that is purely bound (created by `bindService`) is destroyed when its last client unbinds.

questions.question: An app targeting Android 8+ declares a `<receiver>` in its manifest. Which broadcasts can still reach it when the app isn't running?
options: `ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED`
`ACTION_LOCALE_CHANGED`
An explicit broadcast sent to that receiver's component (or with `setPackage`)
`ACTION_POWER_CONNECTED`
`ConnectivityManager.CONNECTIVITY_ACTION`
questions.explanation: Since Android 8, manifest-declared receivers can't get most implicit broadcasts. A short exemption list includes boot completed and locale changed, and explicit broadcasts are unaffected. Power connected isn't exempt. Connectivity changes need a context-registered receiver or a `NetworkCallback`, or WorkManager constraints.

questions.question: An app targeting Android 14 registers a receiver at runtime for its own custom action `com.example.SYNC_DONE`, which only the app itself sends. How should it register?
options: `ContextCompat.registerReceiver(context, receiver, filter, ContextCompat.RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED)`
`ContextCompat.registerReceiver(context, receiver, filter, ContextCompat.RECEIVER_EXPORTED)`, so the system can deliver it
`context.registerReceiver(receiver, filter)` with no flag, since flags only apply to manifest receivers
Use `LocalBroadcastManager`, the recommended in-app event bus
questions.explanation: From Android 14, a context-registered receiver for non-system broadcasts must pass `RECEIVER_EXPORTED` or `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED`. Without one, registration throws `SecurityException`. For in-app-only events choose `NOT_EXPORTED` so other apps can't send it. `LocalBroadcastManager` is deprecated, and a `Flow` is the usual replacement.

questions.question: This toy model mimics `enqueueUniqueWork` with `ExistingWorkPolicy`. What does it print?
options: {sync=[d, e]}
{sync=[a, c, d, e]}
{sync=[b, c, d, e]}
{sync=[e]}
questions.explanation: `KEEP` ignores "b" because "sync" already exists, `APPEND` adds "c", `REPLACE` throws away the existing chain and leaves only "d", and the final `APPEND` adds "e". Real WorkManager behaves the same way for those three policies.

questions.question: An app targeting Android 14 runs a location-tracking foreground service. It has a notification and calls `startForeground()` on time, but the call crashes. What is missing?
options: A `foregroundServiceType="location"` on the `<service>` plus `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`
A call to `startForeground()` from `onBind()` instead of `onStartCommand()`
`FLAG_IMMUTABLE` on the notification's content `PendingIntent`
`START_STICKY` returned from `onStartCommand()`, which Android 14 requires for location
questions.explanation: From Android 14, every foreground service must declare a `foregroundServiceType` and hold the matching `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_<TYPE>` permission. Without the type, `startForeground()` throws `MissingForegroundServiceTypeException`. `START_STICKY` only affects restarts after the process is killed.

questions.question: An app targeting Android 12+ receives a normal-priority FCM data message while in the background and calls `startForegroundService()` to upload a file. What happens, and what is the recommended fix?
options: It throws `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`. Enqueue expedited WorkManager work instead
It works because `startForeground()` is called within a few seconds of starting
The service starts, but the system hides its notification until the app returns to the foreground
The system queues the start and runs the service the next time the user opens the app
questions.explanation: Since Android 12, apps generally can't start foreground services from the background. Only listed exemptions are allowed, such as handling a high-priority FCM message. The documented replacement for short, urgent work is `setExpedited(...)` on a `OneTimeWorkRequest`. Calling `startForeground()` quickly doesn't help, because the start itself is refused.

questions.question: What happens to `process` and `upload` if `DownloadWorker` returns `Result.failure()`?
options: They are never run and are marked `FAILED` too
They run anyway, with empty input `Data`
They stay `ENQUEUED` until `download` is retried manually
WorkManager retries `download` with backoff, then continues the chain
questions.explanation: In a chain, a failed or cancelled work request makes all of its dependents fail or cancel as well. Backoff and retry happen only when the worker returns `Result.retry()`, not `failure()`. On success, each worker's output `Data` becomes the next one's input.

questions.question: Which tasks are a good fit for WorkManager?
options: Uploading crash logs only when the device is on an unmetered network
A nightly backup of the local Room database that must happen even if the app is never opened
Playing a podcast while the screen is off and the user controls it from the notification
Loading the list of products for the screen the user is currently looking at
questions.explanation: WorkManager is for deferrable work that must be guaranteed to run, with constraints like network type, and it survives app exit and reboot. User-visible ongoing work such as playback belongs in a foreground service (`mediaPlayback` type). Data for the visible screen should be loaded with a coroutine in `viewModelScope`.

questions.question: What happens when the user taps the button?
options: It throws `IllegalStateException`: launchers must be registered before `STARTED`
The picker opens and the result is delivered to the lambda normally
The picker opens, but the result is lost if the Activity is recreated by rotation
It compiles but is a no-op, because the launcher is never stored in a property
questions.explanation: `registerForActivityResult` must be called unconditionally during initialization (a property initializer or `onCreate`). Registering in `RESUMED` throws, saying LifecycleOwners must register before they are `STARTED`. Early registration is what lets the result come back to the right callback after recreation or process death.

questions.question: Which statement about `CoroutineWorker` is correct?
options: `doWork()` is a `suspend` function on `Dispatchers.Default`, cancelled when the work is stopped
`doWork()` runs on the main thread, so you must wrap everything in `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` to avoid an ANR
`doWork()` must return a `Result` without suspending, so you need `runBlocking` to call suspend functions
It keeps running to completion even if its constraints stop being met
questions.explanation: `CoroutineWorker` lets you call suspend functions (Room, Retrofit) directly in `doWork()`. It defaults to `Dispatchers.Default`, not the main thread. When constraints are no longer met or the work is cancelled, WorkManager cancels the coroutine, and it will be retried later if needed.

questions.question: WorkManager work survives a reboot and process death, so pending periodic work also keeps running on schedule after the user force-stops the app from Settings.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Work is persisted and rescheduled after reboot or process death. Force stop is different: the OS cancels the app's jobs and alarms, and no work runs until the user launches the app again, at which point WorkManager reschedules it.
